name: The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face

podcast.body: This recording was Billboard's top hit of 1972 and subsequently swept the Grammys at the 1973 awards, winning both Record and Song of the Year. This marked the beginning of a two-year streak where Flack's recordings dominated these categories. "The first time ever I saw your face, 1972's top billboard hit, swept at the 1973 Grammys."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: And the Grammy Goes to… Edition Part 1

podcast.body: This song was the Billboard year-end number one for 1972, a success born from "a series of lucky breaks" for Roberta Flack. This old folk standard, sung at a "smolderingly slow tempo," gained significant traction after filmmaker Clint Eastwood licensed it for his directorial debut, "Play Misty for Me." It became a "late breaking smash," spending six weeks at number one, the most of any song in 1972, and secured the year-end title over Don McLean's "American Pie." "As this old folk standard sung by Flack at a smolderingly slow tempo was licensed by filmmaker Clint Eastwood for his directorial debut Play Misty for Me."
